A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HAVEN framework. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original HAVEN benchmark results, component ablations, iteration analyses and qualitative cases in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and additionally reports runtime comparisons, three-run variance and an alternative-model evaluation.

M1.justification: The audiovisual entity consolidation, four-level database, entity-centric recaptioning, retrieval tools and planner procedure are retained, including the appendix prompt. Newly specified clustering parameters document the existing method; alternative reasoning and inspection models are an evaluation configuration.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LVBench, Video-MME, LongVideoBench and EgoSchema on the same video-understanding tasks. The additional analyses reuse existing coverage; the LongVideoBench change concerns split reporting.

E2.justification: V2 adds DVD as a comparator in the measured average-iteration/runtime analysis in Appendix E, Table 4; v1's average-iteration plot compares HAVEN with Ours_clip. The retained accuracy comparisons use the same baselines.

E3.justification: V2 adds runtime per query as an evaluation metric and tests DeepSeek-R1-0528 for reasoning with Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct for visual inspection. Table 2 drops full-validation LongVideoBench reporting while retaining its long-validation subset. Common sampling rates, dataset counts and planner step limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices E and F add a quantitative efficiency comparison with DVD and a check using open-source reasoning/inspection models. Existing component ablations, category analysis and qualitative cases are retained; moving the speaker-cohesion examples into Figure 3 does not add a new analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix F first reports three LVBench runs and variance of 0.149. V1 provides no comparable run-count or uncertainty reporting. This establishes new disclosure, not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Under unchanged stated settings, Table 2 revises HAVEN's Video-MME score from 85.5% to 82.8% and LongVideoBench long-validation score from 81.0% to 78.2%, without explaining why. Full-validation results, including HAVEN's 83.0%, disappear. V2 adds runtimes of 151.0 seconds for DVD versus 98.7 for HAVEN and an alternative-model accuracy of 75.8%. LVBench, EgoSchema and component-ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The database, entity, scene, tool and memory-update definitions retain their mathematical content. Supplementary Equation 8 repeats the existing toolset definition. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The core contributions and state-of-the-art performance claim are retained. The introduction changes its LVBench example from 81.0% to 84.1%, aligning it with the 2-fps result already reported in v1's abstract and Table 1 rather than introducing a new headline achievement.

C2.justification: V2 expands the explanation of speaker identity's usefulness when visual evidence fails, including motion blur and off-screen speakers. Appendix F newly interprets the three-run variance as robustness evidence. The main ablation interpretations and qualitative explanations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies K1=20, K2=16, agglomerative clustering with threshold 0.4, scene chunk size 24 with overlap 3, and dated GPT-4.1/o3 API versions. These fill implementation gaps without establishing procedural changes. The two-subsegment implementation of 2-fps captioning is retained from v1.

R1.justification: The same 32 cited works and substantive positioning against VLM, RAG and agent approaches are retained. Related-work condensation and publication/venue metadata updates do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction and method undergo extensive rewriting and condensation. Detailed recaptioning and tool descriptions move into supplementary Sections A and B, while the appendix structure changes from A-C to A-G. These substantially reorganize the narrative despite the stable method.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 become compact side-by-side displays, and a new efficiency table is added. V1's appendix Figure 5 moves into the method as Figure 3 with revised labels and caption. The other figure graphics are retained, while the planner prompt table is renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 fills concrete reproducibility gaps with retrieval, clustering, segmentation and API-version details, and adds limited efficiency, repeatability and alternative-model evidence. The rewritten structure also improves access to the central method. These gains are modest: the two revised benchmark scores remain unexplained, full-validation LongVideoBench results are removed, and the new timing and alternative-model evaluations have sparse protocol detail.
